claim: Carry CHECK-059's 99%-removal times, two-coat Ultra-Ever Dry bill and unreproduced P3 ponding; 0.1 kg/m² stays provisional.
source_report_body:
QUESTIONABLE/PROJECTION. MAINLINE-059 complete.

What stays on (a Furmidge drop model calibrated on a measured plate; five finishes): P2's smooth hull keeps 0.014-0.051 kg/m2 after rain with 10 min drainage (upper reading x1.48) and 0.011-0.056 after dew.

P3's film bays sag into dishes under vacuum (024: 9.9 cm crown on 2.32 m bays at R10), so its top bays pond rain. That is 37 kg mean over frame orientations at R10, ranging 5-171 (node on top 55, bay on top 171), and it scales as R cubed.

How fast: an energy balance (checked against 050 and FAO-56) dries P2's residue in 0.2-1.0 h at fair midday and 0.6-7.7 h on a fair morning. Ponds need 65-465 h.

Capacity (own model, cure included): P2 carries 0.1945 kg/m2 in all at R10 ISA and 1.127 at R30. 1 mm floats only at R30 ISA. P3 carries 0.1246 at R10 (052).

Answer: P2 keeps the 0.1 kg/m2 design load and holds it by waiting, at no mass cost. Topcoats add 16-47 kg to save 8-17 kg; heater film adds 503 kg.

P3 carries 0.1 kg/m2 only if its ponds are emptied: with a bay on top, R10 sinks (210 against 157 kg). The cheapest fix is to put a node on top and tip the hull past 14 deg after rain. A night shelter (about 4.9M RUB, floor-scaled) is the fallback.

Ground it by weighing a full-scale P2 panel and a sagged P3 bay after rain and dew. 12 NFI.
numerical_scope: Synthesis of attributed reports; consult named check/review findings for numerical disposition
qualification: Its WVTR 0.08 assumption, desiccant capacity, kinetics and unweighed hardware are not an assembled seven-day demonstration. The 059 pond values were not reproduced; both proposed pond routes remain surrogates. Bulk drying is not complete drying.
